title: Honey Lime Chicken Tray
seoTitle: Honey Lime Chicken Tray | Firefighter Meal
shortDescription: Glazed chicken with roasted peppers and red onion on one sheet
subtitle: Glazed chicken with roasted peppers and red onion on one sheet
description: Bone-in chicken thighs roast with bell peppers and red onion, brushed with honey-lime glaze until sticky and golden at the edges.

steps.title: Gather ingredients and equipment
steps.instruction: Line up every ingredient for Honey Lime Chicken Tray in the order you will cook — measure spices into ramekins, trim proteins on a dedicated board, and set tongs, thermometers, and hotel pans within arm's reach before any heat goes on.

steps.title: Preheat ovens and surfaces
steps.instruction: Preheat ovens, griddles, or grills to recipe temp before the crew arrives — cold equipment extends cook time and dries out batch chicken. Confirm burners ignite evenly and sheet pans are greased or lined.

steps.title: Heat oven and prep vegetables
steps.instruction: Heat oven to 425°F. Toss peppers and onion with 2 tbsp oil, salt, and pepper until evenly coated and lightly glossy. Plan about 8 minutes for this step at crew scale. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Season chicken
steps.instruction: Pat thighs dry. Season with chili powder, salt, and pepper. Arrange skin-side up on two half-sheet pans with vegetables around edges.

steps.title: Initial roast
steps.instruction: Roast 18 minutes without glaze until chicken skin starts to render fat and turn lightly golden at the edges. Bake until the center reaches a safe internal temp (165°F) and edges look set — use a thermometer at the thickest point. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

steps.title: Glaze and finish
steps.instruction: Whisk honey, lime juice, garlic, and remaining oil. Brush over chicken and vegetables. Roast 10–12 more minutes until glaze bubbles and temp hits 165°F.

steps.title: Verify safe internal temps
steps.instruction: Spot-check the thickest pieces with an instant-read thermometer — target 165°F. If any piece reads low, return it to heat immediately rather than holding under temp on the line.

steps.title: Hold for call interruptions
steps.instruction: If tones drop mid-service, cover finished food and hold at 140°F in a warm cabinet or 200°F oven — never leave proteins below 140°F for more than 30 minutes cumulative. Note the hold time on the pan with a grease pencil.

steps.title: Portion and open the line
steps.instruction: Portion Honey Lime Chicken Tray onto sheet trays or hotel pans for family-style service. Stack plates, forks, and napkins at the end of the line so late-arriving crew can self-serve without bottlenecking the cook.

steps.title: Rest and portion
steps.instruction: Rest 5 minutes. Peppers should be tender with slight char; chicken juices should run clear, not pink, when pierced at the bone. Keep a backup tray at 200°F for firefighters returning from a call — never serve picked-over pans to late crew. Work in batches if the pan or grill crowding steams food instead of browning — rookies should watch for pale surfaces and adjust heat early.

proTips: Watch glaze in last minutes—honey burns quickly above 425°F.
Serve with extra lime wedges for crew who want sharper acidity.
Swap thighs for drumsticks using same timing if that is what is in the walk-in.
leftovers: Slice chicken into salads with avocado and remaining peppers.
Shred into wraps with the sticky pan glaze as sauce.
whyCrewsLikeIt: Sweet-tart flavor wakes up a tired crew. One tray means less cleanup after a long shift.
mealPrepNotes: Mix glaze ahead in a jar. Line pans with foil for faster cleanup. Station: Brush glaze during last 10 minutes only—early application burns sugar. Station: Rotate pans halfway for even caramelization in a crowded station oven. Station: Rest 5 minutes before slicing so glaze sets instead of running off the tray.
